41201.en: This section is based on the work `On the Nine Intersections of Two Cevian Triangles (Article 20) <https://people.bath.ac.uk/masgcs/bradley.html>`__, by Christopher J. Bradley (with symmetrical notations by César Lozada).
re: X_41201 = isogonal conjugate of the isotomic conjugate of X_41195
X_41201 = polar conjugate of the isotomic conjugate of X_32619
no: This preamble and centers X_41202-X_41224 were contributed by César Eliud Lozada, Februry 05, 2021.

*Let U, X be two distinct points on the plane of ABC, neither on its sidelines nor on a line parallel to a sideline through the opposite vertex. Let* :g:`A_{u}B_{u}C_{u} << A_u B_u C_u >>` and A_{x} B_{x} C_{x} *be the cevian triangles of U and X, respectively. We introduce the nine intersections of these two triangles:*
A_{1} = B_{u}C_{u} ∩ B_{x}C_{x}, and cyclically B_{1}, C_{1}
A_{2} = A_{u}B_{u} ∩ A_{x}C_{x}, and cyclically B_{2}, C_{2}
A_{3} = A_{x}B_{x} ∩ A_{u}C_{u}, and cyclically B_{3}, C_{3}

*Then, assuming that* U = \(u : v : w\) and X = x : y z (barycentrics): A, B_{1}, C_{1} are collinear on a line \(a_{1}\); B, C_{1}, A_{1} are collinear on a line \(b_{1}\); C, A_{1}, B_{1} are collinear on a line \(c_{1}\). BC, B_{2}C_{2}, B_{u}C_{x} concrr in a point A'; CA, C_{2}A_{2}, C_{u}A_{x} concur in a point B'; AB, A_{2}B_{2}, A_{u}B_{x} concur in a point C'. BC, B_{3}C_{3}, B_{x}C_{u} concur in a point A"; CA, C_{3}A_{3}, C_{x}A_{u} concur in a point B"; AB, A_{3}B_{3}, A_{x}B_{u} concur in a point C". A', B', C' are collinear on a line L' and also A", B", C" are collinear on a line L". Moreover, these two lines are concurrent with UX at a point O(U,X), here named the **Bradley bicevian point of (U, X)**. Barycentric coordinates of this point are O(U, X) = u^2*y*z-x^2*v*w : : . In other words, O(U, X) is the U-Hirst inverse-of-X = X-Hirst inverse-of-U (see the **ETC glossary** (``glossary.html``)). A, A_{2}, A_{3} are collinear, as are B, B_{2}, B_{3} and C, C_{2}, C_{3}. The last result means that ABC, A_{2}B_{2} and A_{3}B_{3} are perspective by pairs with common perspector Q(U,X) = (v*z+w*y)*u*x ::. :g:`A_{1}B_{1}C_{1} << A_1 B_1 C_1 >>` is perspective to these triangles: ABC, :g:`A_{u}B_{u}C_{u} << A_u B_u C_u >>`, :g:`A_{x}B_{x}C_{x} << A_x B_x C_x >>`, :g:`A_{2}B_{2}C_{2} << A_2 B_2 C_2 >>` and :g:`A_{3}B_{3}C_{3} << A_3 B_3 C_3 >>`. Let Q_{2} (U,X) and Q_{3} (U,X) be the perspectors of :g:`A_{1}B_{1}C_{1} << A_1 B_1 C_1 >>` with :g:`A_{2}B_{2}C_{2} << A_2 B_2 C_2 >>` and :g:`A_{3}B_{3}C_{3} << A_3 B_3 C_3 >>`, respectively. Q(U,X), Q_{2} (U,X) and Q_{3} (U,X) lie on a line, here named the **Bradley bicevian axis of (U, X)**, whose trilinear pole has barycentric coordinates: T(U, X) = (x*v^2*z-y^2*u*w)*(x^2*w^2-z^2*u^2)*(y*w^2*x-z^2*v*u)*(y^2*u^2-x^2*v^2) : : Note that :g:`A_{1}B_{1}C_{1} << A_1 B_1 C_1 >>` is the side-triangle of the U- and X-cevian triangles. For shortening, the term **side-of-cevians-of-(U,X)** will be used here for this triangle.

The appearance of (i, j, k) in the following list means that the trilinear pole of the Bradley bicevian axis of (X(i), X(j)) is X(k): * (1, 2, 4589), (1, 3, 41206), (1, 4, 41207), (1, 6, 4584), (2, 3, 41208), (2, 4, 22456), (2, 6, 41209), (3, 6, 2966), (4, 6, 41210)
